verified_findings.finding: The canonical daemon-side resume contract defines RESUMABLE_STOP_REASONS as only operator drain-stop and graceful SIGTERM/SIGINT. Source comments and _rearm_operator_drain_for_resume explicitly state that planner-declared completion and operator hold describe work semantics and must remain authoritative/disabled.
verified_findings.scope: Source-level behavior at the pinned public commit.

verified_findings.finding: start_project_daemon(..., resume_continuous=True) uses a broader predicate: any disabled nonempty continuous objective whose done_reason lowercased starts with 'operator ' is re-enabled. That predicate includes an operator hold even though daemon boot explicitly says operator hold must never be resumed.
verified_findings.scope: Reachable by source semantics; no live production exploit was executed.

verified_findings.finding: The Web start path performs write_continuous_config(enabled=true, objective=current objective) before checking active daemon capacity. The function can therefore durably re-enable campaign state and only afterwards return admission_required without spawning the daemon.
verified_findings.scope: Exact statement about code ordering. It does not establish that this failure has occurred in production.

verified_findings.finding: write_continuous_config increments generation under a file lock but does not compare an expected prior state. A full compare_and_swap_continuous_config primitive exists in the same module and checks all continuous-state fields including generation. The rearm paths audited here use the non-CAS writer.
verified_findings.scope: This is an authorization/freshness property, not a claim that file writes are non-atomic. The writer itself uses atomic replacement and locking.

verified_findings.finding: upgrade_project_daemon reads the continuous state before stopping the daemon and, after a successful stop, restores enabled=true and the pre-stop objective through write_continuous_config when that snapshot had been enabled. It does not condition this restoration on the then-current continuous generation/objective/done_reason.
verified_findings.scope: A concurrent semantic change between snapshot and restoration is therefore source-reachable as a stale-resurrection hazard; occurrence frequency is unknown.

verified_findings.finding: A scheduled daemon-upgrade request persists resume_continuous plus a copied objective. Completion validates installation source and daemon process identity, but when the daemon is stopped it restores the request-time objective through non-CAS write_continuous_config. The request is not bound to the current continuous generation, objective, done_reason, or exact disabled state.
verified_findings.scope: Process identity fencing is present and remains a positive control; the gap is campaign-state authority/freshness rather than process-identity validation.

supported: Web start has broader rearm semantics than daemon boot.
Web start can mutate continuous state before admission succeeds.
Immediate and scheduled upgrade restore copied objective state without an exact continuous-state CAS.
A unified exact-state reconcile/rearm boundary is justified by the observed source-level authority split.
sharpened: The highest-value concrete mismatch is operator hold: daemon boot explicitly treats it as non-resumable work semantics, while Web start's 'operator ' prefix can re-enable it.
The strongest ordering defect is that an admission-denied Web start can still leave the campaign re-enabled because rearm occurs before capacity admission.

scope_guards: No live exploit or crash/race was executed.
No production incidence rate is inferred.
The finding does not imply write_continuous_config lacks file locking or atomic replacement; it specifically lacks expected-state CAS semantics.
Process-identity checks in scheduled upgrade are real positive controls and are not being dismissed.
The proposed remediation remains an adaptation/design proposal until implemented and tested.
verification_conclusion: At Argus public commit 33da786bbc6787a2eeb63a5f492498eae87c78c7, continuous-campaign rearm authority is inconsistent across entry points. Daemon boot admits only the two explicit process-stop reasons and explicitly preserves operator hold, while Web start re-enables any 'operator ' reason before daemon-capacity admission. Immediate and scheduled upgrades can also restore request/pre-stop objective snapshots with a non-CAS writer despite an exact CAS primitive being available. This supports an exact-state reconcile/rearm boundary, but proposed creation-stamp/route-fingerprint mechanics remain unimplemented and unmeasured.
